post_message: Reaching zero-dose children. Diagnosing missed vaccination opportunities. Engaging schools and communities on the importance of vaccination to help those who need it most.   Fellows in the latest cohort of the COVID-19 Recovery for Routine Immunization Programs Fellowship — supported by Sabin’s Boost Community and the World Health Organization — tackled these lofty goals and more.   Through this fellowship and their membership in Boost, participants made lasting impact in their communities, connected with peers around the world, and learned lessons they will take forward into the rest of their careers. "You cannot recreate the complexity of an outbreak in a laboratory. By embedding rigorous science into real-world response efforts — under strong ethical and regulatory oversight — we can help build the evidence needed to strengthen future preparedness."  For Sabin President of Research & Development Kelly Warfield, 2025 was a year of progress,  preparedness and partnership. Her first full year at the organization included tripling the R&D team size and doubling the number of Phase 2 clinical trials for Sabin's vaccine candidates for Marburg virus disease and Sudan virus, a strain of Ebola.  And then, just as the team was getting ready to celebrate the end of year holidays, Ethiopia's Minister of Health called and requested Sabin's help responding to the country's first-ever Marburg outbreak. Partners in the #GlobalHPVConsortium work with local organizations every day to #EliminateCervicalCancer and #PreventHPV. Here, VillageReach takes over our account with #SocialWithSabin as part of #CervicalCancerAwarenessMonth, sharing a success story from #Nigeria ⤵️  --  Enugu has stood out as a top performer among all South-Eastern Nigerian states in driving HPV vaccine uptake, with 99% coverage as of October 2025, and our partners at the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) have recognized the progress there, especially around key efforts like Maternal, Newborn and Child Health (MNCH) Weeks.  🔥 How we did it:  Townhall-style dialogues brought people together — moms, teachers, chiefs, religious leaders, and young people — to talk honestly about HPV and the vaccine, where questions were welcomed and fears were respectfully unpacked through:  ✨ Trust: Health workers broke down the science, teachers explained school delivery logistics, and local leaders tied health protection to family and faith. ✨ Action: Caregivers and adolescents who wanted the adolescent to receive the vaccine were linked to on-site vaccination teams. ✨ Partnership: Together with the NPHCDA and local health agencies, Enugu communities kept HPV vaccination visible and accessible, with state leadership setting the direction. We supported school-based delivery and church-based sensitization to build comfort and confidence about the HPV vaccine among girls and those around them. "Global health is not standing still — it is rebalancing. If we stay focused on evidence, equity, building trust, and country leadership, this moment of reshaping can be a foundation for a stronger, more resilient immunization ecosystem to protect lives and prevent deaths around the world."  Sabin President of Global Immunization, Rebecca Martin, joined the organization in mid-2025, at a moment when global immunization was under significant strain. In response to the challenges, her team made strategic pivots, stayed focused on where they can have the greatest impact, and continued building on the credibility, scientific rigor, and local partnerships that have always defined Sabin's work.  Read Rebecca's reflections on finding direction in a disrupted global immunization landscape ⤵️ https://bit.ly/3Lj8W4t

"Unlike COVID-19, there is no commercial market for a Marburg vaccine. Demand is limited to outbreak response, health workers, and emergency stockpiles. Progress depends almost entirely on public sector and philanthropic investment. Sabin’s role is to ensure that lack of commercial viability does not translate into lack of protection."  Sabin Vaccine Institute CEO Amy Finan reflects on a defining moment in 2025 — when #Ethiopia's Ministry of Health reached out for support as the country faced its first-ever outbreak of #Marburg virus disease.   Having responded to a Marburg outbreak in Rwanda the year before, the Sabin team moved quickly — building on established partnerships and lessons learned to support the national response, while generating evidence to support the development of our investigational cAd3-Marburg vaccine.  Read more ⤵️ https://www.sabin.org/resources/2025-spotlight-reflections-on-outbreak-response-and-generating-meaningful-data/   #OutbreakResponse

"When things come every year like influenza, people start getting used to them and tend to forget to vaccinate. People should be aware that the risk is there every year. Unfortunately, we need a new vaccine annually because the virus continues to change, and we must update the vaccine to update our immunity."   Have you had your #flu shot this year? Read our conversation with bacteriologist and Sabin Gold Medal winner Rino Rappuoli, and learn why it's a must. ⤵️ https://www.sabin.org/resources/influenza-is-nothing-to-sneeze-at/
